label: conj:reeb-linking-cwf-normalization
title: CWF linking normalization: the pn-bond amplitude is the unit-normalized exchange-channel component, $\ell(z)^2\,(1+z^2)=z^2$
html:
Conjecture (CWF linking normalization). Let K be a field containing the bond-factor algebra, with [2]_v = v + v^{-1} invertible. There is a linking-amplitude assignment \ell : K \to K on bond factors such that

  \ell(z)^2\,\bigl(1 + z^2\bigr) \;=\; z^2

for every bond factor z, and the physical pn-bond magnitude is g = \ell(z) evaluated at the Markov bond factor z = 1/[2]_v.

The equation states, square-root-free, that the amplitude is the unit-normalized transverse component \ell(z) = z/\sqrt{1+z^2} = \sin(\arctan z): the bond strand's direction in the two-channel Temperley–Lieb decomposition is (1, z) — the direct channel with amplitude 1 and the exchange channel with the Markov conditional-expectation weight z = \delta^{-1} — and the Gauss–Călugăreanu–White–Fuller linking integrand reads that direction through unit tangents per unit arc length. The tangent identification is the Markov property (a theorem); the sine normalization is the CWF unit-tangent structure (a theorem); what this conjecture asserts is the remaining physical identification: the Reeb linking amplitude is the CWF functional evaluated on the channel-space direction.

Consequence (proved conditional on this conjecture)

Given the class, the pn-bond magnitude satisfies the deformed-criticality equation of the criticality proposition: g^2\,(1 + [2]_v^2) = 1, equivalently g^2\,(5 + (v - v^{-1})^2) = 1.

Scope of the conjecture

It does not supply the MeV unit for the deuteron binding law: the linear B(^2\mathrm{H}) = 5g rule remains a near-match with its unit anchor open. No instance of the class is provided, and axiomatisation is not proof, so nothing here is carried downstream.
heading: Conjecture
